problem:
Given that $f(x)=-x+3,$ on which of the following intervals is $f(x)$ invertible?

- $x\in (-\infty ,\infty )$
- $x\in (0.5,\infty )$
- $x\in [-3,\sqrt{2}]$

feedback.problem:
Given that $f(x)={x}^{2}+2,$ on which of the following intervals is $f(x)$ invertible?

- $x\in (-2,2)$
- $x\in [0,\infty )$
- $x\in (-\infty ,0]$
feedback.worked_solution:
The graph of the function $f(x)={x}^{2}+2$ can be obtained in the following way:

- Take the curve $y={x}^{2}.$

- Translate it by $2$ units up to get $f(x)={x}^{2}+2.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932058/assets/ff3d1ac7500d83574b8671b23e99d4a0f1dbd6ab9cebc906aa06ff2c21f95345.png)

A function is invertible on a particular interval if and only if it's a one-to-one function on that interval. To determine the intervals on which the function is invertible, we use the horizontal line test.

- The function $f(x)$ is not invertible on the interval $x\in (-2,2).$ On this interval, some horizontal lines will intersect the curve more than once.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932058/assets/a71ce036adc5dc0b15fce9e367a0c8512699dc6a7814f4e9a1886696d2abad6e.png)

- The function $f(x)$ is invertible on the intervals $x\in [0,\infty )$ and  $x\in (-\infty ,0].$ On these intervals, any horizontal line will intersect the curve at most once, no matter where we draw the line.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932058/assets/6858bd1fab8d9659c84fa941cd63ee9f509c8364dce0e753706c640ecfe6e9ec.png)

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only".
